text:
Alex Chen: hey all :wave: I'm Alex (joining infra team). Trying to get access to Vault + our KMS for some onboarding tasks (dev DB creds, test stripe keys). Who do I ping and what's the minimal request flow? Also curious about rotation windows so I don't accidentally request something permanent.
Maria Gonzales: welcome Alex! :tada: quick checklist for secrets access:
- fill the onboarding secrets form: https://redwood.internal/onboarding/secrets (select team: infra)
- add yourself to Okta group `secrets-readers` (DevEx can auto-add after form)
- open an eng-security ticket if you need write/unseal/KMS-crypto roles
- for dev work request short-lived leases not long-term static keys
Tom Nguyen: <@Alex Chen> short answers from security side:
- read-only vault paths are common and approved via the form. write/unseal/KMS use needs manager + eng-security approval.
- rotation policy: app service secrets rotate every 90 days by default, but developer CLI leases are short (typically 1h to 24h). If you need a longer TTL explain why in the ticket.
- exceptions: include justification + approver name. we try to avoid permanent plaintext secrets.
Maria Gonzales: tooling notes:
- after approvals you'll get a Slack DM from DevEx Bot with instructions.
- to fetch a secret (dev CLI) use something like:
```
vault kv get -field=value secret/team/infra/dev-db
```
- for KMS ops we gate via GCP IAM + KMS key binding. if you need the crypto key role we require a ticket.
DevEx Bot: Hi Alex — I created a placeholder workflow for your request. Steps:
1) submit the form (link above)
2) attach your manager's approval email to the ticket
3) wait for eng-security review (expect ~1 business day)
Helpful links: https://redwood.internal/docs/secrets/onboarding and https://redwood.internal/docs/secrets/rotation
Alex Chen: awesome, thanks y'all. I'll submit the form now and ping here when the ticket is created.
Maria Gonzales: perfect. ping @Tom Nguyen if you need a faster review and include "onboarding: alex chen" in the ticket title.
Tom Nguyen: noted. also if you're testing locally prefer the dev-sandbox creds (TTL 4h) instead of production keys. we can grant that faster.
Alex Chen: got it — requesting sandbox creds first. thanks :thumbsup:
